section_summary.extract_value: This section describes use of the 10-item Upward Physical Appearance Comparisons Subscale (O'Brien et al., 2009), scored 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree) with item scores averaged so that higher scores indicate stronger tendencies to make upward appearance-based social comparisons. The authors state that, in this study, they omitted additional subscales to reduce participant burden and because upward (vs. downward) comparisons are theorized and empirically shown to be more potent for body image.
section_summary.evidence_source: 'Participants completed the Upward Physical Appearance Comparisons Subscale, containing 10 items (e.g., "I compare my body to people who have a better body than me") rated from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree.'; 'In this study, we did not include the additional subscales of this questionnaire to reduce participant burden, and given that upward (vs. downward) appearance-based social comparisons are theoretically and empirically more potent for body image (Festinger, 1954; Myers & Crowther, 2009).'
